In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of anoxia on the levels of glucose, lactate, and glycogen in brain and blood of newborn mice.
the effect of anoxia in the neonatal period, a time when the brain is especially vulnerable to anoxia and hypoglycemia.
the effects of anoxia on the glucose levels of the blood and the brain of newborn mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, during anoxia in the newborn mouse, the brain does not obtain its full glucose requirement from the circulation.
, in the newborn mouse at least, the blood glucose level is a poor indicator of the brain glucose level during anoxia.
, in the newborn mouse, the blood-brain glucose relationship is altered by anoxia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain glucose reserve in the newborn is small and is easily depleted.
anoxic stress is associated with a decrease in brain glucose levels, an increase in brain lactate, and a rise in blood lactate.
the blood glucose concentration is a poor index of brain glucose in anoxia, and that glucose administration may be life saving under these conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucose administration to newborns with hypoglycemia is not a bad idea.
the brain glucose reserve may decrease rapidly in anoxic conditions and that this decrease may be unrelated to the plasma glucose levels.
the brain is not just an organ that is dependent on blood glucose levels, but it is also capable of generating its own glucose through a process called glucoseogenesis.
